messages:
anjali: FYI customer Acme just put a hard requirement in the contract: they want auditable event delivery that proves integrity for all admin/tenant actions for 7 years. asking whether sampled events are OK or they need full streams. also asking if signed bundles with KMS/HSM-backed signatures are viable and what SLA we can commit to for delivery.
maya: TL;DR: sampling is a no-go for FedRAMP-like asks. SOC2/ISO might accept sampling + strong sampling rationale, but FedRAMP-ish customers typically want full, signed trails. we need to scope options.
priya: +1. For HIPAA/BAA customers we must preserve PHI-redaction records and access logs. any event that touches PHI needs deterministic retention and chain-of-custody. sampling would break that.
raj: technically we can do 2 patterns: (A) continuous signed event stream to customer's S3 (server-side encrypted with their CMK) + per-archive signature (HMAC with KMS/CloudHSM) or (B) periodic signed bundles (daily/hourly) with manifest + signature. both need jitter-safe ordering keys and event sequence numbers.
sam: product question: do customers want live validation APIs (push us their validator to run against our stream) or post-delivery acceptance tests? both have UX implications.
leo: legal: if they demand signed bundles and acceptance tests, that becomes part of the SLA. we should set clear acceptance criteria (schema version, delivery window, failure modes and remedies). penalties for missed deliveries need to be capped. also need to map what constitutes "evidence" vs "supporting logs" for contract.
chris: minimal event set we should guarantee: user_id, actor_role, action_type, resource_id, resource_type, model_version, request_id/correlation_id, request_payload_hash, response_hash (or redaction token), timestamp, schema_version, sequence_number, tenant_id, event_source (api/console/internal). plus optional: geo, ip, reason_code, reviewer_id.
anjali: should we expose an "evidence.validation" field that flags whether the event passed internal integrity checks prior to signing? customer asked for proof of signing key's provenance.
maya: good idea. also track kms_key_id and signature_alg and signature_value in the bundle manifest. and include a signing_cert_fingerprint if we use cert-backed HSM.
chris: example event (minimal):
```json
{
  "schema_version":"1.2",
  "ts":"2024-11-20T18:02:03Z",
  "tenant_id":"acme-corp",
  "actor":"alice@acme.com",
  "actor_role":"admin",
  "action":"grant_role",
  "resource":"project-42",
  "request_id":"req_01E5T...",
  "model_version":"gpt-open-13b-v2",
  "payload_hash":"sha256:abcd...",
  "sequence":123456
}
```
maya: if we change schema we need backward compatibility rules and a migration path customers can opt into. major versions only for incompatible changes; keep a 'deprecated_fields' map in the manifest.
raj: KMS integration notes: we can support customer-managed keys (CMK) for envelope encryption of the bundle, but HSM-backed signing for attestation needs us to offer either (1) our key in HSM with a signed attestation to the customer, or (2) cross-account HSM signing where the customer's HSM signs a hash we hand off. option (2) is more secure but operationally heavier.
priya: compliance note: for FedRAMP-style audits customers usually require tenant-scoped evidence that demonstrates non-repudiation. they often want the signer key material to be either customer-owned or independently audited. prepared statements from our HSM vendor may not fully substitute for customer CMKs.
anjali: what about real-time alerts if the event stream deviates (missing seq, duplicates, schema mismatch)? customer asked for detection + 1-hr SLA to notify.
maya: we should provide per-tenant health metrics + webhook for anomalies. also make an incident playbook entry linking missing events to potential data loss and forensics steps.
leo: contract language suggestions: define "Evidence Delivery SLA" with (a) delivery window (e.g., daily bundles available in customer's S3 by 06:00 UTC), (b) integrity guarantees (signed manifest + sequence continuity). list exclusions (force majeure, customer misconfig). define remediation (retransmit within X hours, credit cap per month). require acceptance test harness to be run within Y days of onboarding to certify format.
sam: ops question: onboarding flow should include: sample events, schema contract, acceptance harness, KMS exchange (if CMK), and test run proving a signed bundle. we should provide a one-click 'provision audit exports' in Console.
raj: vuln triage tie-in: if an incident causes gaps in audit trails, we must escalate to Sev1 and run a signed forensic export. include retainment of raw ephemeral logs for 90 days for forensics even if customer retention is longer.
priya: ensure redaction metadata is included: what was redacted, reason_code, redactor_id, redaction_method. that helps HIPAA auditors.
anjali: customer also asked whether we can validate incoming acceptance tests automatically and provide a signed 'acceptance receipt' after successful run. good to have for contracts.
maya: engineering estimate: baseline MVP for this (bundle signing, manifest, S3 delivery, schema v1.0, console toggle) = 3 sprints. cross-team: infra (KMS/HSM), sec (schema + attestation), product (console + SLA text), legal (contract language).
leo: I'll draft a short contract addendum template for Evidence Delivery SLA and acceptance criteria. will loop back once we have the exact schema.
anjali: created internal ticket #SEC-4521 to track scope and next steps. @auditbot can you create the customer-facing FAQ and onboarding checklist?
auditbot: Ticket created: SEC-4521 (Audit exports & signed evidence onboarding). link: https://redwood.internal/SEC-4521 :rotating_light:
sam: next steps: maya + raj + priya + leo meet tomorrow 10:00 to finalize schema and options. I'll put a calendar invite.
anjali: thanks everyone. I'll reply to the customer with interim options (signed daily bundles or live stream + validation) and timeline.
maya: leave a note: keep sampling out of the default policy for regulated tenants unless legal signs off.
